Definition: of uncertain origin; an adder or other poisonous snake (literally or figuratively):--viper.
BiblicalUsage: A viper is a poisonous snake, and John the Baptist and Jesus both use it as a name for people whose religion is a cover for poison. John calls the Pharisees a generation of vipers and asks who warned them to flee the wrath to come, and Jesus says the same to the Pharisees whose words are full of evil. In Acts the word turns literal again, when a viper fastens on Paul's hand on Malta and he shakes it off unharmed.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe words reveal the heart the way a snake's bite reveals its venom, and religious language is no antidote. Only a changed heart makes the speech safe, and God is the one who changes it.
